name: Head & Neck
tagline: Where sensing, thinking and speaking begin.
description: Everything you think, say, taste and recognize happens here. Your skull houses the brain and the sensory organs, while the face carries the muscles that let you smile, chew and speak. The mandible is the only freely movable bone in the head, hinged to the skull and driven by powerful chewing muscles. Below it, the neck is a crowded corridor: the cervical spine supports the head, the pharynx and larynx share the route for food and air, and the thyroid gland and major vessels sit close to the surface. That density is what makes the region fascinating. A small volume holds the control center for the entire body, twelve pairs of cranial nerves, and the airway you depend on every second.

name: Chest & Thorax
tagline: The moving cage that guards your heart and lungs.
description: Your thorax is a cage with a job: protect the heart and lungs while staying flexible enough to breathe. The sternum and ribs curve around to meet the thoracic spine, forming a barrel that expands with every inhale. Inside, the lungs flank the heart, which sits slightly left of center and pumps blood through vessels that enter and leave the chest. The diaphragm seals the bottom, pulling downward to draw air in. Everything here is synchronized: the heart's rhythm, the lungs' inflation, and the pressure changes that move blood and air together. Notice how alive the region feels. You can feel your heartbeat through the chest wall, watch your ribs rise, and hear your own breath. It is also the body's most protected space, wrapped in bone and muscle for good reason.

name: Abdomen
tagline: A soft workshop of digestion, storage and quiet chemistry.
description: Below your ribs and above your pelvis lies the busiest workshop in the body. The abdomen holds the stomach, liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, kidneys and the coiled small and large intestines, organs that work together to break down food, absorb nutrients, filter waste and manage fuel. Most are wrapped in peritoneum, a slippery membrane that lets them slide over one another as you move, bend and breathe. The abdominal wall, layered with muscle, holds everything in place and helps you cough, lift and steady your spine. What makes this region remarkable is its range: the liver alone performs hundreds of jobs, the gut hosts trillions of microbes, and the kidneys fine-tune your blood chemistry minute by minute. Much of it happens without sensation, a constant hum of work you never notice.

name: Pelvis
tagline: A bony basin where the trunk meets the legs.
description: The pelvis is a basin of bone that does two jobs at once: it carries the weight of your upper body and it cradles organs low in the trunk. The hip bones, sacrum and coccyx lock together into a ring, with the pubic symphysis and sacroiliac joints holding the circle closed. Inside, the bladder and rectum, and in some bodies the uterus and ovaries or the prostate, rest in a space shaped by ligaments and pelvic floor muscles. Those floor muscles act like a sling, supporting the organs and helping control urination. The region is where the trunk hands its load to the legs, which is why its angle and stability matter when you walk, run or sit. It is one of the most mechanically interesting parts of the skeleton: a ring, a passage and a platform at once.

name: Upper Limbs
tagline: Built for reach, grip and delicate control.
description: Your upper limbs are a study in range and precision. Each starts with the shoulder girdle, the clavicle and scapula, which floats over the ribcage and lets the arm swing through an extraordinary arc. The humerus, radius and ulna form the arm and forearm, and the wrist and hand carry twenty-seven bones that allow a thumb to meet each fingertip. Muscles rarely work alone here: shoulder muscles position the arm, forearm muscles turn the hand, and small intrinsic hand muscles fine-tune grip. Nerves from the brachial plexus thread through the armpit and down the limb, delivering touch, strength and coordination in one package. What makes the region compelling is its trade-off: mobility over stability. You can scratch your back or thread a needle because the shoulder gives up rigidity for reach, and the hand turns that freedom into delicate work.

name: Lower Limbs
tagline: Columns built for standing, walking and running.
description: Your lower limbs carry you through the world, and every part is shaped by that job. The femur is the longest and strongest bone in the body, set into the hip socket at an angle that places your knees under your center of gravity. The tibia bears the weight below the knee, the fibula stabilizes the ankle, and the foot's arch spreads force across dozens of bones. Muscles work in opposition and partnership: the gluteals drive your hips, the quadriceps straighten the knee, the calf lifts you onto your toes, and the arches absorb and return energy with each step. Standing still is work too, a quiet balancing act of small adjustments. The result is a system built for load and travel, sturdy enough to carry you for decades and springy enough to run.

name: Whole Body
tagline: All systems, one continuous living design.
description: Step back and the body reads as one system rather than a collection of parts. Skin wraps the whole surface, bone gives it a frame, and muscles pull on that frame to move it. Blood travels a closed loop, carrying oxygen from the lungs, nutrients from the gut and signals from glands, while nerves carry the messages that coordinate the timing. None of these systems runs alone. Your heart rate responds to your muscles' demand, your breathing adjusts to your blood chemistry, and your kidneys and skin help keep the internal environment steady. What is most striking is the scale of the cooperation: trillions of cells, dozens of organs, and feedback loops that hold temperature, pH and hydration within narrow limits. Anatomy, seen whole, is less a list of parts than a single coordinated design.
